name: Liberal Kemalism
summary: Liberal Kemalism reads Atatürk's republican revolution through liberal commitments: secular republicanism and a civic Turkish nation, combined with individual freedoms, multi-party democracy, private enterprise over etatism, and equal rights for women. Its best-known formulator Ahmet Ağaoğlu criticized the Republican People's Party's one-party authoritarianism while still sharing the Kemalist belief in modernizing society from above.
scope: The strand of Kemalism associated with Ahmet Ağaoğlu and the 1930 Free (Liberal) Republican Party of Fethi Okyar, built from the 1924 constitution, Ağaoğlu's writings as described by scholars, and the party's reported programme. Answers are for a committed modern adherent of that strand; it excludes the statist and military-guardian mainstream of Kemalism and later conservative-liberal Turkish parties. Many answers are inferred because few sources record this strand's positions in detail.

sources.title: Kemalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Six principles, laicism, populism against class conflict, republicanism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Ağaoğlu's later welfare-state thinking included publicly funded health and education, on the model of the New Deal, so state-guaranteed care fits.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The sources describe welfare provision but say nothing of wage floors; liberal Kemalists lean market-friendly yet welfarist, so adherents plausibly split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Free Republican Party favoured private enterprise over state enterprise and an end to monopolies, but Ağaoğlu disliked Anglo-Saxon laissez-faire, so the agreement is moderate.

public-ownership.rationale: The liberal wing opposed etatist state enterprise and wanted private initiative, so broad public ownership of industry is not its line.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources give no tax-progressivity stance; the party sought lower taxes overall while Ağaoğlu backed welfare spending, so this is a genuine split.

unions-good.rationale: Early Kemalism rejected class conflict and the liberal strand does not make unions a theme, so no stated position exists.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1924 constitution lists property among natural rights but allows expropriation for public interest with prior compensation, so it is a strong but not absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Atatürk's quoted view was that markets should not be intervened in without necessity but none is wholly free, which leaves regulation level unresolved.

cut-welfare.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported pensions and social benefits, so cutting welfare as dependency-creating conflicts with his outlook; inferred for modern adherents.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is a socialist model alien to a private-enterprise party that rejected class politics; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The tradition prizes individual liberty yet also state security; sources do not address surveillance, so adherents are split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses drug policy; a modernizing, order-minded Kemalist outlook leans against full legalization, though liberals may differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The constitution limits liberty only where others' rights are affected, which could cut either way for hate speech; no direct source.

strong-leader.rationale: Ağaoğlu condemned the CHP's one-party authoritarianism after 1926 and argued for multi-party politics, so bypassing gridlock via a strong leader is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberal Kemalism is a state-founding republican creed with a vigorous state reforming society; anarchist rejection of the state is far outside it.

limit-guns.rationale: The sources are silent; a modernizing republican tradition with a state arms monopoly leans toward strict regulation by inference.

empower-police-military.rationale: Liberal Kemalists criticized authoritarian abuse yet venerate the republic's military heritage; adherents are split with no stated position.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No source touches the question; liberal individualism and conservative republican morality pull in opposite directions.

decide-locally.rationale: Kemalism's unitary republic and centralized reform favour national over local authority, and Ağaoğlu shared the belief in transforming society from above. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

rehabilitation.rationale: The constitution bans torture and corporal punishment, and a reformist Enlightenment outlook leans to rehabilitation; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Ağaoğlu pushed gender equality and women's independence and wanted secular morality rather than tradition, though he valued the family for social ends.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed historically; modern liberal Kemalists divide between liberal individual rights and conservative nationalist social norms.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; secular modernism and women's autonomy suggest support, but Ağaoğlu's pronatal mother-centred framing keeps this low confidence.

more-religion-public.rationale: Laicism is a core principle: keep religion out of government, curb the clerical establishment and subordinate religion to the state.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Race-based remedies don't map onto a civic doctrine that treats all citizens as equal Turks; inferred and split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed; Ağaoğlu argued for women's equal role but framed it around social function, so no clear view on this theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ağaoğlu helped found the Turkish Hearths and held that the Turkish nation must be built on its historical and cultural origins.

gradual-change.rationale: Kemalism is reformist and Jacobin, imposing rapid change from above against established religious institutions, and Ağaoğlu shared its top-down modernization.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; civic definition of Turk is inclusive but the tradition is protective of national homogeneity, so inferred split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Free Republican Party sought closer ties to the League of Nations, but sovereignty was held to rest unrestrictedly with the nation, so views conflict.

free-trade.rationale: The party's programme favoured openness to foreign capital and fewer monopolies, supporting freer trade though not as doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Atatürk's maxim was peace at home and abroad, balancing national interest with cooperation; adherents split on the framing.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The sources never cover intervention; Kemalism's non-expansionist foreign policy and Western orientation point in opposite directions.

open-borders.rationale: A nation-state tradition with Turkish national identity and sovereignty makes open borders unlikely even for liberals; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Modernizing developmentalist tradition seeks growth through private enterprise and capital inflow; degrowth is unaddressed and unlikely.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no source addresses climate, and modern liberal Kemalists are mixed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Kemalism claimed a basis in science and reason and pursued modernization, so technological optimism is inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; neither principle nor documented adherents settle this.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kemalism itself arose from a revolution and Ağaoğlu compared it to the French one, yet liberal Kemalists reject later violent overthrow of the republic. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

experts-over-public.rationale: Ağaoğlu valued meritocracy but held liberties should have an educative function, a paternalist element offset by his democratic criticism of the CHP. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

central-planning.rationale: The Free Republican Party rejected statist economics and constant state intervention in favour of private enterprise.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public or worker ownership is not part of a private-enterprise programme; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source supports a single land tax; the party sought lower, broad-based taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Ağaoğlu opposed inherited privilege and favoured meritocracy, yet the party defended private property; no stated tax position.

basic-income.rationale: Ağaoğlu's welfare ideas were pensions and public services, not unconditional cash; unaddressed so inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The party welcomed foreign capital and opposed statist intervention; protection was the etatist line it dissented from. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of investment is the etatism that the liberal wing opposed in favour of private enterprise.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The 1924 constitution protects property generally and populism stressed national unity, with no stated view on distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A private-enterprise, anti-collectivist programme rejects abolition of money and wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A liberal-economy programme in a modernizing state would not abolish central banking; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Kemalist populism rejected class conflict and favoured national unity, which has a corporatist flavour, but the liberal strand opposed state-run bodies; split leaning against.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized one-party abuses in a 1926 report to Atatürk and wrote the programme for an opposition party seeking multi-party democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Republicanism is a founding principle; the monarchy and caliphate were abolished and replaced by elected officials.

democracy-best.rationale: The Free Republican Party aimed at multi-party democracy, though Ağaoğlu saw liberties as educative, so support is firm but qualified.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1924 constitution made the Assembly the sole representative of the nation; referendums were not part of the tradition.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the base of power is a socialist model rejected by a republican, parliamentary, anti-class-conflict tradition.

right-to-secede.rationale: Kemalism builds a unitary indivisible nation-state whose single Turkish political identity covers all citizens.

natural-rulers.rationale: Ağaoğlu stressed meritocracy over inherited privilege and the 1924 constitution abolished group and family privileges.

political-violence-never.rationale: The republic was founded through a war and revolution while liberals oppose repression; no firm position.

war-builds-character.rationale: Atatürk's foreign policy stressed peace at home and in the world, so glorifying war is inconsistent.

separate-church-state.rationale: Laicism keeps religion out of government, though in practice the state controlled religion through the Diyanet rather than strictly separating them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Kemalist laicism replaced religious law with secular codes and removed Islam's legal role.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A state-founding republican tradition treats justice and defence as state functions; the constitution vests them in state organs.

military-superiority.rationale: The doctrine of peace abroad conflicts with arms-race language but Kemalism prizes a strong army; split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Article 88 defines Turk as a political term including all citizens, and Kemalist nationalism is civic not ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Kemalist populism explicitly rejects class conflict and collectivism in favour of national unity.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The liberal wing stresses equality before the law and meritocracy rather than equal results. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The unitary civic model gives all citizens equal status without group land rights; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources do not discuss reparations; Turkey was itself an empire's heir, leaving no clear stance.

civilizational-union.rationale: Kemalism turned away from Ottoman and Islamic unity toward a Western-oriented national state.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ağaoğlu treated egoism as the problem of Eastern societies and prized mutual aid and altruism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Ağaoğlu saw individual and state with mutual obligations but also natural individual rights; the constitution lists natural rights first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed by any source; no firm inference.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Kemalism is a modernizing project that sought industrial and Western progress.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Modernization was central to Kemalism but disruption-tolerance is not discussed; split.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources never discuss bodily enhancement, and the question is anachronistic for a 1920s-30s reform creed, so no position can be inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Ağaoğlu's liberalism stressed accountable, transparent politics and individual rights; handing decisions to algorithms is anachronistic and inferred negative.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is anachronistic for this ideology and no source speaks to it, so neither side can be inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Kemalism broke with the Ottoman past and aimed at progress toward Western lifestyles.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Atatürk described his creed as based on science and avoided dogma, but the tradition also has six formal principles; split.

direct-action.rationale: Liberals pursued change via a legal opposition party and press, not direct action. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

means-match-ends.rationale: The question is not addressed; the tradition accepted top-down means for liberal-ish ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A modernizing, progress-oriented creed that aimed at Western-style development rejects a return to hunter-gatherer life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolishing the division of labour is a utopian-communist aim that a private-enterprise modernizing programme has no place for.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist principle opposed by a creed that rejected collectivism and class politics.

production-for-use.rationale: The liberal wing favoured private, profit-driven enterprise over the planned production-for-need that the statement describes.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Kemalist populism rejects class conflict, and the liberal wing champions private enterprise.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejects class rule and collectivism; Ağaoğlu rejected both fascism and communism for Turkey.

collective-farming.rationale: A private-enterprise, anti-collectivist tradition opposes collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: This Marxist thesis opposes a creed that rejected class analysis and favoured open trade and foreign capital. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

taxation-theft.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed state-funded pensions, health and education, which require taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Article 68 says the only limits on liberty are those protecting others' rights and liberties.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The constitution protects individual natural rights, yet Ağaoğlu's liberalism was communitarian and nationalist, so group rights are not fully excluded. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

conscription.rationale: Kemalism's national army and republic rest on universal military service and Turkey kept conscription; adherents accept it. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Ağaoğlu stressed political voice and parties; exit as the main check is not part of the tradition.

state-as-business.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized lack of transparency and nepotism but thought the state had social obligations beyond business logic.

positive-liberty.rationale: His welfare-state turn paired liberty with public pensions, health and education.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not discussed; the tradition values universities and the press as modernizing, so it rejects the framing.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Civic Turkishness, equality regardless of race and the Enlightenment orientation reject racial determinism.

organic-representation.rationale: The 1924 constitution made the Assembly sole representative of the nation, individually elected; Kemalism abolished corporate estates.

total-state.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected fascism and communism and defended individual freedom of thought against the state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Kemalism did aim at national revival from Ottoman decline, but without a decadence narrative of the radical-right sort; split.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Atatürk's foreign-policy motto was peace at home and peace in the world, which excludes expansion as a national goal. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Republican sovereignty rests on the nation and the Assembly under Articles 3 and 4, not on personal oaths between lords and followers.

bound-labor.rationale: Article 73 and 70 protect labour and ban forced servitude-style practices; incompatible with liberal rights.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Kemalism claimed science and reason as its basis, which is opposed to the view that all knowledge reflects who holds power. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

universal-morality.rationale: Ağaoğlu drew on French Enlightenment and republican thought seeking secular sources of morality.

single-common-good.rationale: Populism stressed national unity, but liberals accept competing parties; split leaning pluralist.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and modern liberal Kemalists hold varied views, so no firm position is stated.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources never discuss a right of return for diasporas, so adherents' views are unrecorded.

revive-national-language.rationale: Turkish language reform purified rather than revived a dead language; no direct relevance.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of firms by workers and the public is not part of a private-enterprise programme that disliked statist control.

school-vouchers.rationale: Kemalism centralized state education and secular schooling; Ağaoğlu viewed education as a state-led priority.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: A lower-tax, anti-statist, liberal-economy party likely favoured fiscal prudence; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Free Republican party tied political freedom of press and thought to freer private enterprise.

rule-by-example.rationale: The tradition relies on laws and institutions rather than rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The republic arose from the War of Independence and national sovereignty is central, in Atatürk's tradition.

force-without-un.rationale: Peace-abroad foreign policy and support for the League of Nations point against unilateral force. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kemalism claimed science and reason as its guide and fought clerical influence, though it left personal faith free.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Ağaoğlu's welfare ideas are described without reference to who qualifies, so restriction to citizens is neither affirmed nor denied.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements are not discussed in the sources on Ağaoğlu's welfare ideas, so the question is left open.

class-collaboration.rationale: Populism rejects class conflict and stresses national solidarity across classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Kemalism sought to modernize but did not set out to sacrifice museums and heritage. Inferred from Kemalism generally; the sources do not record this strand's view.

dominated-front.rationale: Kemalism sought a Western orientation rather than a bloc of dominated countries.

workers-nation.rationale: Class organization was rejected, yet national organization of workers is not addressed.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported equal economic and political rights for women, so legally distinct public roles for men and women contradict his view.

ban-interest.rationale: A private-enterprise liberal programme embraces credit and foreign capital.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 69 abolishes group privileges and Article 88 includes all citizens.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This Marxist account of the state conflicts with Kemalist populism, which denies class division and stresses national unity.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not discussed in sources on this ideology, so no stated position exists.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The civic definition includes all citizens as Turks, yet Kemalism pursued cultural unification; adherents split.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement conspiracy theory appears in no Kemalist or liberal source and conflicts with reason-based, civic nationalism. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the sources, though pluralist liberals might favour proportionality.

national-mission.rationale: Peace-abroad foreign policy and non-expansionism reject a mission to export its system. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Ağaoğlu spoke of women's backwardness and clerical power as problems but did not frame it as structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Ağaoğlu denounced CHP corruption, nepotism and abuse of power after 1926, which supports an agreeing answer for a liberal Kemalist.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts equality and natural rights; eugenics is not part of liberal Kemalism. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Ağaoğlu valued legal accountability and criticized abuse of power; inferred for past killings.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported welfare provision, so a minimal state is rejected despite liberal leanings.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Discouraging marriage across racial lines contradicts equality before the law irrespective of race and the civic definition of Turk.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Article 69 declares all Turks equal before the law and abolishes privileges.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate about socialism that Kemalism, which rejected class politics, never joined.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources never discuss settler colonialism, and the republic's own founding is not framed that way.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Kemalism replaced religious law with a single secular civil code, adopted from Switzerland.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article 75 says no one may be molested for religion or philosophic convictions.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously motivated ban is contrary to secular modernism and has no place in Kemalist sources. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Laicism centralized education under state control, ending madrasa instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist thesis about the socialist state is opposed to the tradition's rejection of class politics.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Article 3 says sovereignty belongs without restriction to the nation.

trade-surplus.rationale: A liberal programme welcomes open trade and foreign capital rather than mercantilism.

population-transfer.rationale: Civic equality of all citizens and constitutional protection are inconsistent with coerced transfers, though Turkey's history includes the 1923 population exchange. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian axiom that Kemalism, a state-building republican creed, does not endorse, though it shares Article 68's harm limit.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Economic competition is welcome but a struggle between peoples is not; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The founders required the Free Party to pledge to republicanism and secularism; the tradition defends the regime against its enemies.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican vocabulary appears in the tradition, but the sources do not articulate freedom as non-domination, so neutral.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1924 text mentions judicial review and Ağaoğlu criticized parliamentary opacity. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist vanguard party is incompatible with liberal Kemalism, which sought multi-party democracy and rejected class politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Ağaoğlu's welfare orientation exists, but a priority for the poor in law and institutions is not stated in the sources.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy is not addressed in the sources on this ideology, so no position can be inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Kemalism limited class organizing, but liberals protect association; split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources never discuss population and poverty, so the question is left neutral.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Kemalist stress on national unity conflicts with the civic inclusiveness of Article 88. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Filling offices by lottery conflicts with the elected Assembly model of the 1924 constitution and with Ağaoğlu's meritocratic emphasis.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kemalist history includes emergency rule, while the liberal strand defends legal rights, so adherents are split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A liberal economy opposes price controls in principle, but emergency measures were accepted in practice, so adherents split.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Free Republican Party promised freedom of the press and of thought, which contradicts party control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The republic keeps the army under state not party command in principle; liberals oppose party control. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization periods are not discussed in the sources, so neither a long nor a short wait can be inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Capping representatives' pay at a worker's wage is not a Kemalist or liberal position in the sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is not discussed for the Free Republican Party in the sources, so the question is left neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Article 3 says sovereignty belongs without restriction to the nation, which argues against pooling it in a supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The sources do not record a stance on who commands the armed forces, so adherents' views are unrecorded.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church organisation is irrelevant to Islam in Turkey, where the state controls religion through the Diyanet, so it is rejected as inapplicable.

clerical-rule.rationale: Laicism is aimed at breaking the dominance of the traditional religious establishment.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Kemalist nationalism rooted in a war of independence contradicts the call for workers to work for their own government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Article 77 prohibits prior censorship of the press and the party promised freedom of thought, which cuts against moral censorship of art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized the entrenchment of personal and one-party power, so unlimited re-election would be viewed unfavourably. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources do not mention recall of officials, so no position can be inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The party sought closer ties with the League of Nations and the tradition looked West, which favours alliances over ending them. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Abolishing renting contradicts the property rights listed in the 1924 constitution and the party's liberal economy.

people-in-arms.rationale: Kemalism built a professional national army under state command, and an armed citizenry in its place has no basis in the sources. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Modernizing urban reform; Kemalism favoured peasant education but not agrarian romanticism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Atatürk's foreign policy renounced irredentism, so reunification of a nation divided by outsiders is not pursued. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Ağaoğlu prized education and meritocracy, so claiming that educated people are out of touch cuts against his outlook.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Kemalism sought to move Turkey toward Western civilization, which assumes some civilizational path is preferable. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

death-penalty.rationale: Turkey retained capital punishment for decades while liberals dissent, and the sources do not record a view, so adherents split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Secular, modernizing education and gender equality as pursued by Ağaoğlu point to supporting this, though it is inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A creed founded on science and reason and secular state education rejects teaching creationism in public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The sources never discuss pornography, and liberal and conservative-republican instincts point in different directions.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Article 88 defines Turk as a political term covering all citizens, which favours a civic over descent-based approach.

minority-language-support.rationale: Kemalism promoted Turkish as the single language; liberals more open but not stated. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Uniform secular law is a Kemalist principle, so exempting religious minorities from general laws is rejected.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Freedom of thought and individual liberty point to tolerance of nonconformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Openness to foreign capital implies honouring foreign debts, so cancellation is inferred as unlikely.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Atatürk's era valued economic independence but liberals favoured foreign capital.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The sources do not discuss constitution-making methods, so the question is left neutral.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Ağaoğlu opposed authoritarian hardening, though liberties were to have an educative role.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid duties are not discussed in the sources, and the question is anachronistic for the founding period.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The question is anachronistic for the period and not addressed by the sources.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1924 constitution had parliament choose the president; no stance of liberals. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A liberal economic orientation leans toward independent monetary institutions, though the sources do not state it, so it is inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Atatürk renounced irredentism but the republic firmly guards its territory, so a rule against ceding claimed land is inferred weakly.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 74 allows expropriation for public interest but property is a natural right.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The characterization of the Soviet Union is a Marxist debate not addressed by the sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The precautionary principle is modern and anachronistic, with no stance recorded for this ideology.

collective-defense.rationale: The Western orientation of the tradition favours collective defence, though the sources do not state it, so this is inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources do not address the status of territories annexed without consent, so neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Laicism meant the state centralizing religious institutions, abolishing the caliphate and Sufi orders and creating the Diyanet.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not record a stance on a non-partisan head of state, so adherents' view is unrecorded.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The unitary nation-state defends its territorial integrity, so force against secession is accepted as in the Kemalist tradition. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A unitary state does not allow a region to join while keeping its own system, so this is rejected.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The republic replaced the sacral monarchy and caliphate, so regarding the head of state as sacred is rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The party sought lower taxes overall, but no source mentions a flat income tax, so neutral.

character-from-environment.rationale: Ağaoğlu emphasized education, upbringing and social context in his reform thinking.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Article 68 and constitutional rule limit rulers by law, which contradicts a ruler above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is anachronistic and not addressed by the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The republic uses a single sovereign Assembly representing the whole nation rather than mixing few and many, so this is rejected.

leader-cult.rationale: Ağaoğlu opposed personalized one-party power though Kemalist public life honoured Atatürk; liberal strand cooler. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

equal-parenting.rationale: Child custody presumptions are not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This doctrine about class struggle under socialism is rejected by a creed that denies class conflict.

land-redistribution.rationale: The constitution protects property as a natural right and the party favoured private enterprise, so seizing estates is rejected.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not discuss refugee return, so no position can be stated.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Atatürk's peace-abroad, non-irredentist foreign policy rejects claiming territory because co-ethnics live there. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Article 75 says no one may be molested on account of religion, sect or philosophic convictions, so punishing apostasy is rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: Kemalist reforms discouraged religious dress and promoted women's emancipation, so legally requiring cover is rejected.

common-currency.rationale: A shared currency is not discussed in the sources, and sovereignty concerns point in opposite directions, so neutral.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ağaoğlu earlier favoured unity with Azerbaijan, but the republic renounced pan-Turkism. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Kemalism recognized a single national culture and civic nation, so self-governing minority cultural institutions are not endorsed. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources do not discuss minority strategies of this kind, so no position can be inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Kemalism did not adopt Marxist historical materialism, preferring national unity and reform from above.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Free Republican programme called for an end to monopolies, supporting prohibition of cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: The sources do not discuss bank or firm bailouts, so neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The constitution speaks of judicial review and natural rights that majorities should not override, so this statement is rejected. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported gender equality but mandatory parity in public bodies is not discussed, so neutral.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The party's openness to foreign capital and trade rejects an autarkic imperial economic bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade agreements are anachronistic and not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: A private-enterprise programme relies on material incentives, so replacing them with moral incentives is rejected.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The foco theory of revolution is not part of Kemalist thought, which rejected Marxist revolution. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Article 69 abolished privileges of groups, classes and families, and Ağaoğlu favoured meritocracy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Ağaoğlu helped found the Turkish Hearths and held that the Turkish nation must be built on its own historical and cultural origins, which implies teaching its own history first.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The republic was founded by a war of independence against foreign domination, so rule by an advanced power over others sits badly with it, though it admired Western civilization. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

patriotic-education.rationale: Kemalism centralized state education to create a national citizenry loyal to the republic, and Ağaoğlu backed Turkism and education reform as central tasks.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-conscious remedies have no place in a civic doctrine that treats all citizens as equal Turks, but nothing documents a view on preferences, so this is inferred as split.

public-money-creation.rationale: A private-enterprise, liberal-economy programme would leave credit and money to banks and markets; the sources never discuss money creation, so this is inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Free Republican programme assumed that a private-enterprise economy open to foreign capital could grow and cope, the opposite of a collapse thesis. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The republic deliberately broke with the Ottoman imperial past and pursued peace abroad rather than cultivating influence over former provinces. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

delink-world-market.rationale: The liberal wing wanted more tolerance for foreign capital and closer ties with the League of Nations, so economic delinking is contrary to its programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist thesis about class; Kemalist populism denies class division, so an adherent would not endorse it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Article 69 abolishes group, class and family privileges and declares all Turks equal before the law, which points against a right to refuse service by group. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1924 constitution set out natural rights and made amendment require a proposal by one-third and a two-thirds vote, an entrenchment adherents would accept.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The republic overturned the Treaty of Sèvres by war, but the principle of voiding colonial-era treaties is not discussed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Republicanism replaced the Ottoman monarchy with elected officials, so rulers are chosen by election among the national community.

minority-veto.rationale: The Grand National Assembly decides on behalf of the nation as a whole, with no suggestion that a dissenting minority can block a decision. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Ağaoğlu defended constitutional rule and freedom of speech in court and criticized abuses of power, though he sought reform through party opposition rather than rebellion. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1924 constitution makes the Grand National Assembly the sole lawful representative of the nation and says it exercises the legislative power directly (Articles 4-6), with no monarch above it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed by Kemalist sources; a science-based modernist outlook would mostly accept this, so the answer is inferred and weak.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the mainstream modernist view that animals may be used with limited suffering is inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Ağaoğlu opposed inherited privilege yet stressed mutual obligations between individual and state, so a duty of the privileged to the less fortunate is neither clearly affirmed nor rejected.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ağaoğlu was a lifelong politically engaged reformer who wrote opposition programmes and reports to Atatürk, so withdrawal from public affairs contradicts the creed.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim not found in Kemalist sources, whose modernizing project sought to spread education and culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: This Gramscian thesis assumes a ruling class, which Kemalist populism denies in favour of national unity.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory conflicts with a programme that sought foreign capital and integration with the wider economy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Article 88 counts all citizens as Turks, but the early republic favoured the Muslim majority in practice, so adherents may split.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate internal to communist movements, with no connection to Kemalism; neutral by default.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The party welcomed foreign capital yet the republic stressed national independence, so adherents can lean either way.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Atatürk's foreign policy of peace at home and in the world renounced irredentist claims on territory lost after the empire. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The constitution treats all citizens as equally Turks under Article 88 and abolishes group privilege, leaving no basis for descent-based political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected fascism as a model for Turkey, but the republic's founding values are republican and national, not anti-fascist as such.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected both fascism and communism as models for Turkey, which fits a liberal reading condemning both.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A question about US history that Liberal Kemalist sources never address.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Kemalists honour monuments to their own founders, but the sources say nothing about contested monuments generally.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Ağaoğlu's gender concern was women's emancipation, and nothing in the sources speaks to male disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in any source on this ideology.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Kemalism aimed to move Turkey toward Western lifestyles and law, adopting European codes and institutions, so it denies that they suit only one civilization.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army saw itself as guardian of Kemalist principles, but liberal Kemalists criticized authoritarianism, so adherents split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Ağaoğlu wanted women educated and active in public life, but no source addresses paying for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; neither a firm yes nor no can be inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Ağaoğlu stressed meritocracy over inherited privilege, which favours merit-based recruitment to public posts.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The Free Republican programme was more tolerant toward foreign capital than the CHP, so blocking takeovers cuts against it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Swiss-derived civil code ended religious control of marriage and secular reform favoured equality, so ending a marriage without proving fault is plausible; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Under the 1924 constitution the Assembly represents the nation as a whole rather than as binding delegates of constituents.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed state pensions and social benefits, so privately managed individual accounts as the basis are inferred as unlikely.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The constitution lists property among natural rights, so community or national ownership of land with individuals only holding use rights is contrary to it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament was made the sole representative of the nation, and Ağaoğlu criticized parliamentary opacity, so parliamentary budget control is consistent.

single-official-language.rationale: Article 2 of the 1924 constitution makes Turkish the official language, and Kemalist nationalism stressed one common Turkish language and culture.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The party was more open to foreign capital than the CHP, but land is a sensitive national question; inferred and weak.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Equality before the law in Article 69 concerns treatment of persons rather than group outcomes, so liability for unequal outcomes is inferred as unlikely.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; Ağaoğlu's moral writing stressed altruism, but nothing is said about consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The republic's motto of peace at home and peace in the world is incompatible with arming insurgents abroad. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Troop interventions in allied states are contrary to a doctrine of peace and a republic born of resisting foreign domination. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

corporate-influence.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized nepotism and opaque government, but the sources do not discuss corporate lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The liberal party promised press and thought freedom and tolerance of foreign capital, which weighs against restricting foreign funding. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Ağaoğlu tied women's emancipation to better motherhood, but no source documents state incentives, so adherents are split.

residents-only-property.rationale: The constitution lists property among natural rights available to all citizens, which cuts against local purchase limits. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

job-guarantee.rationale: Having the state guarantee jobs is an etatist measure of the kind the liberal wing opposed in favour of private enterprise.

democratic-peace.rationale: The thesis is not discussed in Liberal Kemalist sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A republic built on constitutional law and the rule of law expects obedience to legitimate laws.

non-intervention.rationale: Atatürk's motto of peace at home and peace in the world implies respect for other states' internal affairs. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

industrial-unions.rationale: The organization of unions is not addressed by sources on the ideology.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Equal citizenship under Articles 69 and 88 contradicts conspiracy accusations against a minority. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Civil marriage under the secular civil code was a core Kemalist reform replacing religious marriage, so abolishing legal marriage is contrary to it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized the lack of transparency and parliamentary opacity under CHP rule.

local-production.rationale: A programme tolerant of foreign capital and trade does not stress buying locally. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

informal-organisation.rationale: An anarchist method opposed to a state-building republican tradition operating through parties and formal institutions. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty belongs to the nation, yet the Free Republican Party wanted closer League of Nations ties, so adherents split.

religious-nation.rationale: Article 88 says the name Turk as a political term includes all citizens, defining the nation by citizenship rather than shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The republic was founded by resisting foreign domination and claims unrestricted national sovereignty, so ritual deference is rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Kemalism builds a unitary state with centralized revenue and administration. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The question presupposes common ownership of production, which the party rejected, but personal belongings are uncontroversial; no clear position.

defeat-communism.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected communism as a model, but the sources don't describe an active crusade to defeat it, and Atatürk's Turkey coexisted with the USSR.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed public welfare services alongside a private-enterprise economy, implying a mix; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Laicism curbed clerical power but left private belief free; Atatürk did not declare religion an illusion. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A private-enterprise programme sees business as an engine of modernization; inferred from its economic stance.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ağaoğlu argued for equal economic and political rights for women within the existing order rather than for transforming the economy.

socialized-care.rationale: Not discussed; the tradition's emphasis on women educated for the family and public life makes public socialization of care unlikely.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language reform was a Kemalist project, but liberal adherents differ on how far to purge borrowed words. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

treaties-binding.rationale: The sources do not discuss treaties between governments and nations within their borders.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing cooperative communities are an anarchist-style model far from a private-enterprise republican programme.

majority-settlement.rationale: Equal rights for all citizens under Article 88 argue against encouraging settlement to shift regions' balance, though early Turkish policy included settlement. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected communism and fascism but favoured a market economy with welfare, so he did not seek a third system.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The republic renounced irredentism, but nothing is said about the strength of historical claims in general.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Nothing in Kemalist or liberal sources supports denial, and a reason-and-science creed would reject it; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Article 68 limits liberty only to protect others' rights, and the republic did not criminalize it, though adherents may be socially conservative. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The party was created to give multi-party democracy a platform, and Ağaoğlu criticized the abuse of power under one-party rule.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Article 75 says no one may be molested for religion or philosophic convictions, and a secular state does not enforce religious offence.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The republic was born in anti-imperial struggle and has no overseas colonies; inferred rejection.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Laicism removes religious law from public duty, though Ottoman-era resistance used religious language.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Laicism makes rulers answerable to secular law, so declaring rulers illegitimate for not following religious law is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Ağaoğlu valued democracy but held that liberties should have an educative function, so wide direct participation is not clearly endorsed.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not discussed; Ağaoğlu treated women's oppression and clerical power as problems but did not theorize overlap.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Kemalist populism claimed to transcend classes, but liberal Kemalists place themselves in a centre-right opposition tradition, so adherents split.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept that is alien to a creed rejecting class conflict.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Ağaoğlu aimed to modernize Muslim societies and resisted Western misperceptions of Islam, so he would reject incompatibility.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Article 3 says sovereignty belongs without restriction to the nation, not to God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Laicism meant the hat reform and, later, restrictions on religious dress in state institutions, which most Kemalists support. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern workplace issue not covered by sources on the ideology.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ağaoğlu combined a more liberal economy with pensions, health and education, a market-with-welfare position.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The republic was founded through a war of independence and built a national army, so abolition is rejected. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

rich-first.rationale: The party favoured private enterprise and foreign capital, which tolerates uneven growth, but nothing says so explicitly.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Atatürk's motto of peace at home and peace in the world suggests staying out of great-power blocs, though liberals also valued Western ties. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Republicanism abolished hereditary rule and Ağaoğlu opposed inherited privilege.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A private-enterprise programme tolerant of foreign capital relies on ordinary interest-bearing credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The liberal wing welcomed foreign capital and economic openness, so defying lenders is unlikely; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Article 69 makes all Turks equal before the law, and the republic extended the vote rather than restricting it by wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ağaoğlu's modernism sought women's emancipation through science and education, not an ecofeminist critique. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Hegelian concept not found in this tradition. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The party promised freedom of press and thought and saw them as real under the existing order. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Article 68 allows liberty to be limited only by law, in line with government by publicly announced standing laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Article 69 makes all Turks equal before the law, and Article 88 includes every citizen.

open-government-data.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized opacity in government, so open decision records are inferred as favoured.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The secular civil code replaced religious marriage law, removing religious restrictions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Equality of all citizens under Articles 69 and 88 is incompatible with boycotts by group. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized clerics for harming Islam and sought a modern, secular morality, so he would favour reinterpretation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ağaoğlu opposed inherited privilege and monopolies were attacked by the party, but no source states that wealth endangers liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Laicism meant state neutrality and control of religion, and Atatürk kept private belief free, so promoting atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A state-building republican tradition relies on state order and law enforcement. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: A unitary state with a single civic Turkish identity does not accept communal executive power-sharing. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed state pensions and social benefits, not charity as the main answer.

term-limits.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized entrenched power but the sources never mention term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: The constitution rests on representative sovereignty through the Assembly, so delegation of votes is inferred as unlikely.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Laicism leaves religious office to religions, so the ideology takes no side.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported gender equality and women's independence, and the secular civil code removed male legal authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The constitution ties political rights to citizens; inferred and weak.

rent-control.rationale: Price and rent caps are statist interventions the liberal wing opposed in favour of private enterprise.

abolish-ip.rationale: Abolishing patents conflicts with a private-enterprise programme; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Kemalist state organised youth for national purposes, but liberal Kemalists opposed one-party regimentation. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic for the founding period and not addressed by sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: National sovereignty argues against foreign bases while Western alignment argues for them; adherents split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official Turkish nationalism rejects recognition, and the sources note Ağaoğlu's reported role in measures against Ottoman Armenians, so adherents likely resist; contested.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Ağaoğlu valued merit over inherited privilege but defended a private-enterprise order, so adherents split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Article 68 permits defence of liberty and rights, and no pacifist tradition exists in Kemalism. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ağaoğlu's Turkism stressed historical and cultural origins, but the republic was also a deliberate break with the past. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The republic honours those who died in the War of Independence as national heroes, though not as saints. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Laicism and a science-and-reason basis reject framing politics as a spiritual struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; the republic focused on its own territory rather than being a centre for diaspora culture.

culture-before-state.rationale: Kemalism built the state first and used state power to reshape culture from above. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Equal citizenship and property rights for all citizens argue against reserving economic life for one national group, though early Turkish policy favoured Muslim businesses. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Kemalism preserved a unitary state with provinces set by the centre, not merging regions by ethnicity. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

independent-unions.rationale: The liberal party promised freedom of thought and association, and independence from the state follows; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A Marxist test of socialism that does not apply to a creed rejecting class politics.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed publicly funded health and education, but local utilities are not discussed.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1924 constitution set up a single assembly, and sources don't record the liberal strand's view.

municipal-property.rationale: Local community ownership of the means of production contradicts a private-enterprise programme.

confederal-coordination.rationale: A confederation of self-governing towns contradicts the unitary republic.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; adherents plausibly split between welfare support and equal pay for women.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Ağaoğlu presented the individual and the state as having mutual obligations and defended individual natural rights, though he balanced this with communitarian ideas.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Laicism and a science-and-reason basis make it unlikely that politics is built on human spirituality. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: In a unitary republic, regional powers rest on national legislation and can be changed by it.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Equality before the law and civic citizenship reject racial political blocs.

racial-pride.rationale: A civic nationalism defining Turks by citizenship rather than race treats racial pride as foreign to it. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Atatürk's motto of peace at home and peace in the world points to using armed force only for defence. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Article 88 defines Turk politically as all citizens, though Kemalism also stressed a common language and culture.

communal-electorates.rationale: The unitary civic nation with equal citizens rejects separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Sèvres-syndrome suspicion is common in Kemalist nationalism, but the liberal strand is more open to the West, so adherents split.

free-public-college.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed publicly funded education and Article 87 made primary schooling gratuitous, but college tuition is not discussed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Ağaoğlu valued women's educated role as mothers but also equal rights, so adherents split on whether women bring distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: The party sought closer ties with the League of Nations, but arms reduction is not described in sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: A liberal party seeking transparency in government is inferred to favour open diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: The party was more tolerant of foreign capital than the CHP, so state control of capital movements is unlikely. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The republic holds a monopoly on armed force through its army and police; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: A national republic born of a war of independence does not accept soldiers refusing to fight. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Ağaoğlu's welfare ideas are listed only as pensions and public services, so this specific tool is not addressed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The party wanted lower taxes and less state intervention, but no source mentions binding fiscal rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; the liberal wing sought integration into the existing economy rather than restructuring it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The republic itself is the state built by the Kemalist revolution, so smashing it is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: A unitary state with one national economy does not permit communities to adopt different systems. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

sacred-nation.rationale: Secular nationalism treats the nation as a political community, not a sacred one. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Official Kemalism denied that the centre exploited regions, so adherents reject the thesis. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Ağaoğlu drew on French Enlightenment and republican thought and on natural rights, which presuppose a shared human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: The party promised freedom of press and thought, and independent public media fits that; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

farm-price-support.rationale: The party preferred markets, but farm support is not discussed.

workers-own-party.rationale: Kemalist populism rejects class politics and favours national unity in a single party framework.

ban-fgm.rationale: Ağaoğlu campaigned for the rights and bodily independence of women; inferred support.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported equal economic and political rights for women, and the secular civil code gave women equal inheritance rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Kemalist populism shifted legitimacy away from tribal leaders to citizens, so chiefs in lawmaking are rejected.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Article 68 says liberty is limited only to protect others' rights, which points against subordinating liberty to environmental goals. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Turkish is the official language under Article 2 and Kemalism stressed a common language. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: A liberal programme tolerating private enterprise favours freedom of association, which includes not joining; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by sources on the ideology.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Article 75 protects each sect but the state in practice controlled religion through the Diyanet and favoured one interpretation, so adherents split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The party sought free multi-party elections, but liberals also value liberties, so adherents split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Secular morality and women's equality suggest acceptance; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The party promised freedom of press and thought, so state shutdown of communications is contrary to it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Ağaoğlu's welfare ideas centred on pensions and public services, so this alternative is not addressed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported equal economic and political rights for women, the reasoning being that they must take part in public life.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Ağaoğlu named the backwardness of women and the power of clerics as the two main problems in the Muslim world.

race-social-construct.rationale: The civic definition of Turk makes race irrelevant, but the sources don't state a view on the scientific status of race. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported equality for women but dedicated agencies are not discussed.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The constitution protects property but regulates it by law, rejecting a first-claim homestead doctrine. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The party sought closer ties with the League of Nations, but tribunals for leaders are not mentioned.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Laicism and a science-and-reason basis reject literal scripture as an authority. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Self-government for national groups conflicts with a unitary civic republic. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The liberal wing opposed statist planning and rejected communism as a model for Turkey.

indirect-election.rationale: The 1924 constitution had parliament elect the president, but sources don't record a stance on tiered election.

national-church-status.rationale: Laicism removed Islam's special legal status, though the state kept control of religion through the Diyanet.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The unitary republic with all citizens as Turks leaves no room for territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the 1924 constitution's principle that sovereignty belongs to the nation and from the strand's liberal democratic commitments; the sources record no position on plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the Kemalist 'peace at home, peace in the world' preference for the existing settlement; the sources do not discuss colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the strand's support for private enterprise, foreign capital and modernisation, which treats abundance as good; no source addresses simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the civic Turkish nation and equal rights for all citizens in the 1924 constitution, which sit badly with limits on where citizens may settle.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the strand backs equal rights for women, but the Kemalist republic kept conscription for men only and no source records adherents asking to change that.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from its civic, secular conception of the nation, which treats land as a state territory rather than a sacred inheritance.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The strand stresses individual liberties and constitutional guarantees, as in the 1924 constitution, which do not allow killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its Western-oriented modernizing outlook.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from its civic Turkish nationalism, which defines the nation by citizenship rather than ethnic kin abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its preference for private enterprise and property over state or collective ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: Liberal Kemalism combines Kemalism with individual freedoms and private property, which fits personal rights over body and labour. Inferred from Kemalism generally or from no source; the sources do not record this strand's view.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not address consumption taxes; liberals and welfarists within the strand plausibly differ.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed welfare provision, but the sources do not say whether it was universal or means-tested.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The strand criticized the CHP's one-party authoritarianism and its 1930 party stood for multi-party democracy.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its preference for private enterprise over etatism and its transparency critique of the ruling party.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Secular republicanism and laicism are core to Kemalism and to this strand, so religion is not a basis for parties.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from its drive to modernize society from above, which put modern values ahead of traditional ones.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Ağaoğlu argued for women's equal rights and secular morality, which supports a wife's right to end a marriage.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 1930 programme welcomed foreign capital, so foreign firms developing resources fits; resources are not specifically discussed.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the strand's liberal commitment to private enterprise over etatism; its later welfarism tempers this.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; liberal Kemalists are market-friendly but welfarist, so no clear stance is inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed; the strand's civic, non-ethnic nation concept gives no clear view on racial disadvantage.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the strand's attachment to the constitutional, procedural republic; it criticized one-party practice by constitutional means rather than disobedience.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed; modernizing zeal suggests openness to technology but welfarist concern for employment cuts the other way.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from Kemalism's Western-oriented modernization, which favours integration with Western institutions over a balance of rival civilizations.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the party's private-enterprise liberalism, which sits with market valuation rather than a labour theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Kemalism's populist principle of serving the whole people and its civic patriotism, with solidarity across classes.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not addressed; the strand's concern was liberal freedoms and economic liberalism, not left-wing strategy.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The Free Republican Party was founded to end one-party rule with multi-party competition and private enterprise, so party-led socialism contradicts it.

missingStatements.text: A country's alphabet and writing system may be changed by law to modernize it.
missingStatements.rationale: Ağaoğlu pushed alphabet reform and cultural modernization, a defining Kemalist reform no current statement captures.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow: a one-off Kemalist reform that other ideologies rarely take a side on.

notes: Sources on this strand are thin and partly contested: Wikipedia's Liberal Kemalism article flags unsourced claims, and scholars note Ağaoğlu's liberalism was communitarian and reliant on state-led change. Strict etatist Kemalists would answer economic and state-power statements differently.
